note: Background music the client approved, with the exact timing and levels that were approved. Audio files live in assets/music/ and are NOT committed (the repo is public and these are commercial tracks); on a new machine, ask the client for the file and put it at the 'file' path. Use a track only where 'suits' fits the video, never on 'avoid'. Measured values come from the approved mix.

tyler-gone-gone.title: GONE, GONE / THANK YOU (instrumental)
tyler-gone-gone.rights: Commercial track supplied by the client. Not cleared for paid ads; business accounts may get it muted. Prefer adding it through the platform's music library when posting from a business account.
tyler-gone-gone.start_rule: The file has 103.6 ms of silence before its first hit; trimming 0.1026 s puts the first audible sample on frame 0 (the hook frame). Measured offset in the approved mix: 0.00 ms.

mix.level_rule: Before ducking, the part of the track a video uses is set to the voice's loudness minus 2.7 LU (voice -15 LUFS -> music -17.7 LUFS). That is the approved mix: its 27.3 s segment measured -14.7 LUFS, with -3 dB pre-gain. A fixed gain is not enough: the track's first 10 s are -17.9 LUFS, 3 dB quieter than the rest, so a short video would sit 9 dB under the voice instead of ~7.
mix.under_voice_rule: The bed must sit 6.7 dB under the voice WHILE THE VOICE SPEAKS (50 ms blocks with the voice above -35 dBFS; voice alone vs the bed through the identical chain), as measured on the approved Brooklyn Bridge mix. The loudness match (level_lu_vs_voice) is only the starting point: on the Montgolfier edit (dense speech) it left the bed at 4.8 dB, so mix.py measures and corrects the gain before the final render.

tyler-gone-gone.approved_in: Brooklyn Bridge -> WKC story edit (lab/edit-04, wkc_bridge_v1_music.mp4), 2026-10-17: the client asked for it to be clearly audible; -13 dB with heavy ducking was inaudible.
suits: serious but positive brand or agency promos (WKC)
calm, confident talking-head pacing; 76 BPM, a beat every 0.79 s
videos that open on a strong hook frame (the track starts on a hit)
avoid: paid ads or accounts where commercial music is not cleared
videos whose voice is quiet or busy with dialogue (the bed sits only ~7 dB under the voice)

sinatra-come-fly-with-me.title: Come Fly With Me
sinatra-come-fly-with-me.rights: Commercial recording supplied by the client. Not cleared for paid ads; business accounts may get it muted. Prefer adding it through the platform's music library when posting from a business account.
sinatra-come-fly-with-me.start_rule: Client: the video starts 0.5 s before Sinatra sings "Come fly with me, let's fly, let's fly away". "Come" starts at 10.085 s in the file (forced alignment of the vocal line), so the edit starts at 9.59 s; "away" ends at ~15.10 s (video 5.51 s), so the speaker starts after that.

mix.scheme_rule: Jazz/classy style: the song is automated, not side-chain ducked. Up (about the voice's loudness, -0.5 LU) in the opening line, the interludes between his explaining and the end card; while he talks it sits under_voice_db under the voice with a gentle cut at 1-3 kHz (Sinatra's vocal range) so two voices don't fight. Raised-cosine ramps of ~0.4 s in the pauses: down just before his first word, up right after his last.

suits: flight, travel and aviation stories (the title line is the hook)
edits with music interludes between the explaining
avoid: a constant bed under dense talking (it has vocals)
paid ads or accounts where commercial music is not cleared

echoverse-les-yeux-ouverts.title: Les Yeux Ouverts
echoverse-les-yeux-ouverts.rights: Track supplied by the client; licence not stated. Not cleared for paid ads unless the client confirms the licence; when posting from a business account, prefer the platform's music library.
echoverse-les-yeux-ouverts.start_rule: Client: start from the first real sound. The file is silent for 0.48 s; the first note (a D-minor chord, D-F-A) starts sharply at 0.4816 s (first sample above -60 dBFS), so trimming 0.481 s puts it on frame 0.
echoverse-les-yeux-ouverts.vocals: French, sung-spoken storytelling from 1.74 s after the start ('Dans la grande salle d'un chateau...'); instrumental stretch about 10.0-19.5 s; drums fuller from ~20 s.

mix.scheme_rule: As the Sinatra track: automated, not side-chain ducked; up in the opening, interludes and end card; while he talks 12 dB under the voice with the gentle 1-3 kHz cut (it has vocals); ~0.4 s raised-cosine ramps in the pauses.

suits: storytelling openings (the lyric opens like a tale)
avoid: a constant bed under dense talking (it has vocals)
paid ads unless the licence is confirmed
echoverse-les-yeux-ouverts.note: Sent by mistake for the Eiffel edit; the client wanted Trio Musette's version (trio-musette-les-yeux-ouverts).

trio-musette-les-yeux-ouverts.title: Les Yeux Ouverts
trio-musette-les-yeux-ouverts.rights: Track supplied by the client; licence not stated. Not cleared for paid ads unless the client confirms the licence; when posting from a business account, prefer the platform's music library.
trio-musette-les-yeux-ouverts.start_rule: Client: start from the first real sound. 0.09-0.17 s is a soft noise burst (bellows/air, spectral flatness 0.61, not a note); the first note (G chord) attacks at ~0.266 s and is full by 0.33 s, so trimming 0.262 s puts the note's attack on frame 0.

mix.scheme_rule: Classy style: automated, not side-chain ducked; up in the opening, interludes and end card; while he talks 10 dB under the voice (instrumental accordion musette: less than the 12 dB used for songs with vocals, still a clear swell in the interludes) with the gentle 1-3 kHz cut (the accordion sits in the voice's range).
